newsitem.title: MEXICO: Comerci nears syndicated loan deal.
newsitem.headline: Comerci nears syndicated loan deal.

text.p: Supermarket chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana (Comerci) is in the final stages of closing a syndicated loan for up to $135 million to refinance debt raised in April to pay for its purchase of K-Mart units in Mexico, a company official said on Thursday.

"We're in the process of closing it. It's going to be a syndicated loan which could be up to $135 million, depending on how the syndication goes," Raul del Signo, head of investor relations, told Reuters in an interview.
He said the credit would pay an interest rate around the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) plus 2-1/8.
In April, Comerci paid around $148.5 million to buy K-Mart's Mexican operations. Del Signo said the purchase would bear fruit by the end of the year.
"We've told analysts that even though the second quarter is not going to be so good in operating terms because of the K-Mart purchase, the third and fourth quarters will be better."
He said Comerci would cut the payroll that was a part of K-Mart by 10-15 percent from its level of between 310 and 330 workers over the next five months.
"We're going to take advantage of the high turnover of (shop) floor workers. It's not going to mean eliminating personnel. We hope the workforce will be reduced normally."
He said the company planned to open or remodel several outlets with a remaining investment of $36.5 million this year.
